reason: Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to (nutlet appendages in Boraginaceae, hair-like appendages elsewhere); as with 'segment' and 'lumen' in the 2026-11-13 review, no single class fits without context.

Narrower: the rays of a compound umbel inflorescence (PO_0030130) are its primary branches; PO lists 'primary inflorescence branch' as an EXACT synonym of PO_0006321. Count examples ('Umbel rays 7-13') fit the amount pattern. Apply only in an umbel context; bare 'ray' must not go to ray system PO_0025411 or ray flower PO_0025331.

label: leaf lamina cell
parent: is_a PO_0009002 (plant cell); part_of PO_0025396 (phyllome lamina)
definition: A plant cell (PO:0009002) that is part of the lamina of a leaf (PO:0025396 phyllome lamina), including the one-layered lamina of a bryophyte leaf (phyllid), described by its shape, wall thickening, papillae or transparency.
reason: Moss floras describe the cells of the leaf blade all the time (median, alar, basal cells; pellucid, papillose, rounded). PO has plant cell and phyllome lamina but no class joining them, and the part-of pattern (12) needs a quality on the whole. Should be proposed to PO upstream, with a bryophyte example.
The number of cell layers ('2 layers of cells', '1-stratose') is a thickness or structure quality of the part that has them (exostome tooth, lamina), not a part to annotate.

target: plant anatomical space (PO_0025117) as part of leaf lamina cell (proposed above)
reason: PO_0025117 lists 'lumen' as a synonym. Here it is the cell cavity of moss leaf cells ('lumens irregularly rounded', 'flexuous'). It can be expressed as a part of the leaf lamina cell once that class exists. Bare 'lumen' stays rejected (2026-11-13).
Fragment of a comparison ('1/6-1/4 of the leaf length'): it is a ratio of the bearer's length to the leaf, for pattern 10 (ratio to another part), not a part.

Exact in bryophyte floras: the 'sex organs' are the antheridia (PO_0025125) and archegonia (PO_0025126), i.e. gametangia. 'sex organs ... not seen' is specimen condition (pattern 06) rather than true absence.
The number of turns of a coil or twist ('5 turns', 'faisant 1-5 tours') is a twisted or coiled quality of the bearer (awn, fruit, tendril), not a part.
Quality (how many there are) of the structure it qualifies (cystoliths, nectaries).
Fragment of '-androus' (word trimmed too far). '3-4-androus' counts stamens: add androus -> stamen to the counted-parts table (pattern 03) and do not ground the fragment.
Quality (depth) of lobes or grooves; the counted part is the lobe or groove.
Stem fragment of inflorescence(s), also caught on 'ramifications'; fix the word trimming so the full word grounds to inflorescence PO_0009049 rather than adding a rule for the fragment.
Texture quality of the part it describes (woody rootstock, woody brachyblasts); the bearers are rootstock/rhizome and short shoot, already ruled.
A loose group (young stems, leaves, inflorescences, whatever is not woody) with no single PO class. Shoot system would be too broad and would wrongly include woody stems.
Fragment of a comparison ('1/3-1/2 the length of the lamina'): a ratio of the bearer's length to the lamina (pattern 10), not a part.
Arrangement of veins or roots ('veins forming a network'): a reticulate or anastomosing quality (FLOPO:0991128) of the veins, not a part.

target: lobe counted in plant ovary (PO_0009072): pattern 03 with container ovary, via the 'lobed -> lobe' row of config/flora_counted_parts.tsv
reason: Only counts occur ('5 lobes', 'three lobed ovary'): the count pattern expresses it as the amount of lobes in the ovary, so no new class is needed. 'Trilobed' as a single word stays a shape quality of the ovary.

Exact in floras: 'pubescence of simple hairs' is the indumentum of the part. Do not use PO's seed trichome PO_0004511, which lists 'pubescence' only for seed hairs. The 'stipe 0-3 mm' example is a misparse.
Quality (venation or surface pattern), not a part.
Narrower: a bract subtending a secondary branch or flower group. 'Secondary' is its position in a series, which pattern 04 records on the bract; no new class needed.

label: xylopodium
parent: is_a PO_0009008 (plant organ); part_of PO_0000003 (whole plant)
definition: A plant organ (PO:0009008) that is a thickened, hard, woody underground structure of stem and/or root origin, from which aerial shoots are produced and which persists through drought or fire, as in many plants of seasonally dry savannas such as the cerrado.
reason: A real perennating organ with no PO class: not rhizome (PO_0004542) or tuber, and lignotuber is also missing. Used by neotropical and African floras for its length, branching and presence. Should be proposed to PO upstream, possibly together with lignotuber.
Number word belonging to a count, not a part.
How many times something branches ('branching 8-10 times') is a branched quality of the axis or hair, not a part.

Narrower: PO lists colpus/colpi/sulcus as synonyms of canal; here they are pollen furrows. '3-colpate' counts them on the pollen grain: add colpate/colporate -> colpus to the counted parts. Colporate (a furrow with a pore) is slightly broader.
Colour quality of the marks or spots it describes.

target: shoot system (PO_0009006) with context quality young (pattern 04)
reason: The young shoots of the plant (young stems and leaves). Pattern 04 records the state on the bearer, the same as 'young stems'.
Fragment of a verb phrase ('nerves bearing ... scales'); the scales are the part, and they are already handled by existing bearer rules.

Narrower: an inflorescence of umbel-like clusters that only looks like a compound umbel. Do not map to compound umbel inflorescence PO_0030130, which is the true kind. The inflorescence type itself is a feature of the inflorescence, not a new part.

label: pinna rachis
definition: A stalk (PO:0025066) that is the axis of a pinna of a bipinnate or more highly compound leaf (PO:0020043), arising from the leaf rachis (PO:0020055) and bearing the pinnules.
reason: PO leaf rachis PO_0020055 is defined as the main axis only, and the bearer review prompts say a secondary rachis is not the primary one. The examples (winged, in 4-10 pairs, hairy) fit bipinnate leaves of legumes and ferns. Should be proposed to PO upstream. In an inflorescence context, map to second order inflorescence axis PO_0006321 instead.

Narrower: perigone = perianth (rule C370), and its segments are the tepals ('libres', 'égaux', '3-4-mères'). Where the source says the perigone is fused, they are perianth lobes (FLOPO_0986004, rule C372).
